docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
This repository contains Yocto Project layers and other files for building Linux images for CTEK boards.

If you are not familiar with the Yocto Project, start by reading the overview: https://www.yoctoproject.org/software-overview/

docs.title: Selecting a Hardware Platform
docs.text:
Before you can build any package or image, you must start by sourcing the profile script for one of the supported machines.

Use this command to set up a specific machine

source meta-cs-bsp/board/conf/profile.sh <machine>

Use the following command to list all available machines:

source meta-cs-bsp/board/conf/profile.sh

This has to be done every time you start a new shell from where you want to build using Bitbake.

The first time a profile.sh script is run for a certain board, a new build directory is created, typically named build-{board}, where {board} is the name of the selected target board. In that directory, other files and directories are also created. For the rest of this description, the target board is assumed to be "ccu".

docs.title: Build Configuration
docs.text: One of the files that the profile script creates at first run is build-{board}/conf/local.conf. This file is based on a template in the board directory in meta-cs-bsp. Take a look at it and try to understand what the different settings do. Some of them described in the Yocto Project documentation, here: https://docs.yoctoproject.org/ref-manual/varlocality.html#local

docs.title: CTEK Board Images
docs.text:
In general, there are two classes of images for CTEK hardware - production images and development images. Production images are named "{product}-image" and are the ones that are installed in the factory and released in software upgrade packages.

Development images are named "{product}-dev-image" and contains (almost) everything that the corresponding production image does, plus additional packages and tweaks that are useful during development. A board with a dev image installed also permits logging in with SSH and a simple password, so it is therefore absolutely critical that dev images are not released into the wild.

docs.title: ChargeOS Distribution
docs.text: Since the different images share a lot of packages and configuration options, there is a Yocto Distribution defined in meta-cs-distro/conf/distro/cschargeos.conf, called "ChargeStorm ChargeOS". The local.conf template files for some CTEK boards are set up to use this distro. There is also a GUI variant of the distro that should be used for images targeting chargers with a graphical display.

docs.title: Image Hierarchy
docs.text:
In addition to configuring common options in the ChargeOS distro, board images are also arranged in a hierarchy. The image files are found in meta-cs-distro/recipes/images and meta-cs-proprietary/recipes/images and their relationships are described in the following diagram. Note that images for some boards have been left out for simplicity, but they should follow the same pattern.

@startuml

package "meta-cs-distro" {
    [cschargeos-base-image.inc] as base_image
    note left of base_image
        Adds some open source applications
        and tweaks the distro
    end note

    [ccu-image.bb] --> [base_image] : include
    [cgc500-image.bb] --> [base_image] : include
    [gm-ccu-image.bb] --> [base_image] : include
}

package "meta-cs-proprietary" {
    [cschargeos-base-prop-image.inc] as base_prop_image
    note left of base_prop_image
        Adds CTEK proprietary
        applications and libraries
    end note

    [ccu-image.bbappend] --> [base_prop_image] : include
    [ccu-image.bbappend] --> [ccu-image.bb] : extend

    [ccu-dev-image.bb] --> [base_prop_image] : include
    [ccu-dev-image.bb] --> [ccu-image.bb] : extend+tweak
}


@enduml
  • @mermaid{rfidauth}

docs.title: RFID presented, Session not finalished
docs.text:
Purpose: Session could not get finalised as the EV did not get connected before timeout. - Parameter: ConnectionTimeOut = 180 seconds



sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as Customer
    participant EV
    participant EVSE
    participant Backend as OCPP backend

    User->>EVSE: User presents RFID TAG (123456)
    EVSE->>Backend: OCPP: Authorize.req (idTag=123456)
    EVSE->>Backend: OCPP: Authorize.conf(idTagInfo(status=Accepted)

    activate EVSE 
    EVSE->>Backend: StatusNotificationReq (status=Preparing, connectorId=1)
    Backend->> EVSE: StatusNotificationRsp
    EVSE->>Backend: StatusNotificationReq (status=Preparing, connectorId=2)
    Backend->> EVSE: StatusNotificationRsp
    EVSE --> EVSE:Timeout 180 sec
    deactivate EVSE
    EVSE->>Backend: StatusNotificationReq (status=Available, connectorId=1)
    Backend->> EVSE: StatusNotificationRsp
    EVSE->>Backend: StatusNotificationReq (status=Available, connectorId=2)
    Backend->> EVSE: StatusNotificationRsp
    note over EVSE: Indicate available on outlet 1 and 2

docs.title: UC:EV is connected, Session not finalished as no RFID is presented
docs.text:
Purpose: Session could not get finalised as the EV did not get authenticated before timeout. - Parameter: ConnectionTimeOut = 180 seconds



sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as Customer
    participant EV
    participant EVSE
    participant Backend as OCPP backend
    User ->>EVSE: Plugs in charging cable in outlet 1
    EV ->> EVSE: need to charge (C1)
    note over EVSE: Indicate preparing on both outlet, start ConnectionTimeOut
    activate EVSE 
    EVSE->>Backend: StatusNotificationReq (status=Preparing, connectorId=1)
    Backend->> EVSE: StatusNotificationRsp
    EVSE --> EVSE:Timeout 180 sec
    deactivate EVSE
    EVSE->>Backend: StatusNotificationReq (status=Finishing, connectorId=1)
    Backend->> EVSE: StatusNotificationRsp
    note over EVSE: Indicate Finishing on outlet 1

docs.title: UC:EV is disconnected no RFID tag used
docs.text:
• StopTransactionOnEVSideDisconnect = True
  • Not applicable on fixed cable chargers.
  • outlet/X/keep_cable_locked = False
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as Customer
    participant EV
    participant EVSE
    participant Backend as OCPP backend
    note left of EVSE: Charging session is active
    User ->> EV: stops charging
    EV->>EVSE:do not need to charge (B2, SuspendedEV) 
    EVSE->>Backend: StatusNotificationReq (status=SuspendedEV, connectorId=1)
    Backend->> EVSE: StatusNotificationRsp
    User ->>EV: Unplugs cable from EV 
    EV->>EVSE: enter A2-A1 : Disables PWM
    EVSE->>Backend: StatusNotificationReq (status='Finishing', connectorId=1,errorCode=NoError, info='EV side disconnected'.)
    Backend->> EVSE: StatusNotificationRsp
    alt UnlockConnectorOnEVSideDisconnect = True and 

    EVSE ->>EVSE: unlocks connector on EVSE side
    end 
    EVSE ->> Backend: OCPP: StopTransaction.req(transactionId=XXXX, reason= EVDisconnected, .. )
    Backend-> EVSE: OCPP: StopTransaction.conf ()

docs.title: UC:EV is disconnected no RFID tag used
docs.text:
• StopTransactionOnEVSideDisconnect = False
  • When a Charge Point is configured with StopTransactionOnEVSideDisconnect set to false, a transaction is running and the EV becomes disconnected on EV side, then a StatusNotification.req with the state: SuspendedEV SHOULD be send to the Central System, with the 'errorCode' field set to: 'NoError'. The Charge Point SHOULD add additional information in the 'info' field, Notifying the Central System with the reason of suspension: 'EV side disconnected'. The current transaction is not stopped.
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as Customer
    participant EV
    participant EVSE
    participant Backend as OCPP backend
    note left of EVSE: Charging session is active

    User ->>EV: Unplugs cable from EV 
    EVSE->>Backend: StatusNotificationReq (status=SuspendedEV, connectorId=1,errorCode=NoError, info='EV side disconnected'.)
    Backend->> EVSE: StatusNotificationRsp
    alt UnlockConnectorOnEVSideDisconnect = True
    EVSE ->>EVSE: "unlocks connector on EVSE  /n                      1"
    end
